segments.text:
V. 23
When he was come into the temple, the chief prieſts came—Who thought he violated their Right: And the elders of the people—Probably, Members of the Sanhedrim, to whom that Title moſt properly belonged: Which is the more probable, as they were the Perſons under whoſe Cognizance the late Action of Chriſt, in purging the Temple, would naturally fall. Theſe with the Chief Prieſts, ſeem purpoſely to have appeared in a conſiderable Company, to give the more Weight to what they ſaid, and if Need were, to bear an united Teſtimony againſt him. As he was teaching—Which alſo they ſuppoſed he had no Authority to do, being neither Prieſt, nor Levite, nor Scribe. Some of the Prieſts (tho' not as Prieſts) and all the Scribes were authorized Teachers. By what authority doſt thou theſe things?—Publickly teach the People? And drive out thoſe who had our Commiſſion to traffick in the Outer Court?
